searchText: For users who are more price sensitive, but not time sensitive, is there a risk of setting the maxFeePerGas closer to the baseFee, like say `maxFeePerGas = (baseFee * 1.2) + maxPriorityFeePerGas` or even `maxFeePerGas = baseFee + maxPriorityFeePerGas`. Currently building out settings for metamask and would like to provide a reliably cheap option for users who have non-time sensitive transactions. We will have to wait for 1559 to launch to see what miners set for the minimum premium, but assuming they are economically rational it should be between 1 and 5 or so. Once we have more data you can look at the history of inclusion and figure out what their settings are. For launch, I'm recommending people set like `2` until we have more data. This means you would have `maxFeePerGas = (baseFee * x) + 2` or something. Personally, if you have users who are price conscious I really think the best thing to do is just ask them "what is the most you are willing to pay to include this transaction" and use that for `maxFeePerGas`. There is no reason to set the `maxFeePerGas` to lower than what you are willing to pay. You should basically *always* set that to be equal to your willingness to pay. Understood, it was more that the multiplier `2` in the suggested default of `maxFeePerGas = (baseFee * 2)` seemed like a large range of possibility for some users. Was wondering what the logic behind suggesting that default was. um, thanks, but this is the 1 example I already posted. Not trying to be annoying but it would really be helpful to have examples for tests! It was also difficult last time with eip-2930 and then a million things were broken when it actually went live, so some more examples and tests would be clearly a good idea, thank you This is one such risk I guess that avoids https://twitter.com/vdWijden/status/1410023932527263745?s=20 Since there's an increased risk of your transaction being kicked now, so a higher multiple also takes that risk into account. So in addition to pending for a long time, a low `maxFeePerGas` also has an increased risk of your transaction being dropped. It is a tradeoff between quoting the user a price that "astronomically high" and "likely to not be included in the next block. 2x feels like it is a nice sweet spot of "most users will accept a fee that is within 2x of their willingness to pay (unlike say 10x)" and "it is very likely the transaction will be included in one of the upcoming blocks". If the timing is serendipitous, two basefee rises might happen in the time between: - seeing the fee - clicking accept - approving on hardware wallet So if the broadcast tx is based on a basefee from two blocks in the past, the protocol basefee might be 1.125*1.125 = 1.27x their submitted basefee. For this reason alone, submitting with fees around this multiple or less could cause some frustration now and then sorry, it's the only one i had seen myself dumb me for not reading your full post - noticed you had it right there Which format would work best for you? I can generate some transactions if you need Most of the transactions send by my account here: https://ropsten.etherscan.io/address/0x6177843db3138ae69679A54b95cf345ED759450d are 1559 transactions (type 2) This is a list of similar accounts which send a lot of eip1559 transactions https://github.com/MariusVanDerWijden/go-snippets/blob/7bea173c0a0217ba88fd627322d76f3db4ba1e8e/livefuzzer/addresslist.go#L117 Marius beat me to it, thanks for jumping in! perfect, thank you!!

excerpts.author: perama
excerpts.content:
If the timing is serendipitous, two basefee rises might happen in the time between:

- seeing the fee
- clicking accept
- approving on hardware wallet 

So if the broadcast tx is based on a basefee from two blocks in the past, the protocol basefee might be 1.125*1.125 = 1.27x their submitted basefee. 

For this reason alone, submitting with fees around this multiple or less could cause some frustration now and then
